title: The Door That Looked Like Home

shots.visual_event: Door Three opens onto Arin’s warm family kitchen at sunrise; his mother cooks while Meera laughs, wearing her locked teal coat.
Arin drops his ticket and runs to them; his mother embraces him with convincing warmth.
Saira stays at the threshold. In a steel kettle reflection, the room is an empty carriage and the family have no faces.
shots.dialogue_audio: Saira: “Ask Meera what she warned you.”

shots.visual_event: Arin asks. The smiling Meera repeats the wrong line while the room subtly resets to the same gesture.
Arin tears his brass station badge from the vision; the kitchen peels away into paper-thin clockwork panels.
shots.dialogue_audio: Arin: “My sister told me not to open the door.”

shots.visual_event: The false mother becomes Nila for one quiet second, not monstrous—only hurt.
shots.dialogue_audio: Nila: “I only built the home you wanted.”
